name: Taurine
short: A meta-analysis of 25 trials found no significant adverse effects versus control. A risk assessment found strong evidence of no adverse effects up to 3 g/day; data above that were insufficient.
text: In a meta-analysis of 25 randomised trials (1024 participants; 0.5 to 6 g/day for 5 to 365 days), no significant adverse effects of taurine were observed compared with the control group, and a smaller meta-analysis of seven studies (103 participants) of isolated oral taurine reported no adverse events. A quantitative risk assessment of human trial data found no systematic pattern of adverse effects and judged the evidence for the absence of adverse effects to be strong at supplemental intakes up to 3 g/day in healthy adults; higher intakes had been tested without adverse effects, but the authors considered those data insufficient for a confident conclusion about long-term safety. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
